clue.text: On blacklist, a so-called piece of music, creation of 22

indicators.note: so-called says the words only sound like the first part when spoken, not spelt like it

parts.note: anything on a blacklist is banned; with a, said quickly, BANNED A
a snatch is a short fragment of a tune

explanation.surface: A tune ends up on a blacklist, the work of some author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so-called' signals a homophone: BANNED A, said quickly, gives BANDER, then SNATCH, a fragment of a tune. 22 is CARROLL, so this is a creature of Lewis Carroll's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bandersnatch is a frumious monster invented by Lewis Carroll in his nonsense poem and The Hunting of the Snark.

clue.text: In political draft, article time after time referring to two parties

indicators.note: In tells us the following pieces sit within the draft legislation

parts.note: a bill is a draft law put before parliament
a is the indefinite article
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A political draft keeps referring to an article about two parties, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time after time' asks for two different words for time, one after the other, both inside the draft.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilateral agreements or talks involve two sides, the Latin root meaning two-sided.

clue.text: See 10
Head east, the wrong way, to reach city on the Ruhr

indicators.note: the wrong way says the joined pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Inverness
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Someone sets off east but goes the wrong way trying to reach a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way' turns NESS plus E around.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr valley, home of the Krupp steelworks.

clue.text: Draw on fortune to produce weapon

parts.note: to smoke a cigarette is to draw on it
a bomb is slang for a large sum of money, as in 'costs a bomb'

explanation.surface: Someone draws on luck and comes up with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortune' is British slang: something that costs a bomb costs a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb releases a cloud for cover or signalling, and counts as a device of combat.

clue.text: Total steered out of it

parts.note: to total figures is to add them up
to steer is to lead, past tense led

explanation.surface: A car is totalled because the driver was out of it at the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of it is confused and muddled in the head, which is what addled describes.

clue.text: Whale swallowing old boat

indicators.note: swallowing says one piece goes down inside the other

parts.note: to whale is to thrash, as is to cane

explanation.surface: A whale swallows an old boat whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whale' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light, narrow paddled vessel.

clue.text: 22's menacing beast mopping up duck and orange juice with sponge

indicators.note: mopping up has the outer word soak the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: to bum is to sponge off others, scrounging
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A monster sops up a spilled breakfast of duck and orange juice with a sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sponge' is the verb to scrounge, giving BUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boojum is the deadly variety of Snark in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark.

clue.text: Black music, for example, in order for composer

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
music is one example of an art
something in order is OK

explanation.surface: A composer seeks black music to put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a 20th-century Hungarian composer and folk song collector.

clue.text: Chick egg, by the look of it, left in rain

parts.words: egg, by the look of it
parts.note: O is egg-shaped

indicators.note: in places the letter for left within the word for rain

parts.note: rain makes things wet; wet also means rainy weather

explanation.surface: A chick and an egg are left out in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so a chick of that bird.

clue.text: Where British hikers might go wild in a wood, then race over mountain into 22's quarry?

indicators.note: into says the middle pieces are placed inside the creature's name

parts.note: Carroll's poem The Hunting of the Snark makes the Snark the quarry

indicators.note: over here means the race comes ahead of the mountain
go wild says these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a nation is a people or race
an Alp is a mountain

explanation.surface: Hikers lose themselves in a wood, then race up a mountain hunting a fictional beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wild' rearranges IN A WOOD as OWDONIA. 'over' just means ahead of in this mixed across-and-down entry. The Snark is the beast hunted in Carroll's poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowdonia National Park in North Wales is a celebrated walking region where British ramblers head.

clue.text: Note, bit lower?

parts.note: a jot is a tiny bit
down means lower

explanation.surface: A musical note pitched a little lower.
explanation.definitionFit: To jot down is to write a quick note of something.

clue.text: Fire, for example, in electrical component?

definitions.meaning: fire is one of the four classical ...
the heating coil in a kettle or oven

explanation.surface: Fire breaks out in an electrical part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses use one word: a classical elemental substance, and the resistive heating part of an appliance.

clue.text: Tango in ballroom dancing, women's ultimate hit?

indicators.note: in places the tango letter inside the rearranged dance hall
dancing says the letters of ballroom move about

parts.note: T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: At ballroom dancing, the tango is the women's biggest hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges BALLROOM as MORALBLO; 'in' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mortal blow is a fatal strike, the final hit after which there is no other.

clue.text: A lot bad, so a lot to repair

indicators.note: something needing repair is broken, so these letters must be put back together differently

explanation.surface: Plenty is broken, so there is plenty to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to repair' rearranges A LOT BAD SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Boatloads is an informal expression for a large quantity.

clue.text: See 10
Previously mentioned area, if so shabby, beginning to decay

indicators.note: shabby suggests something knocked about and out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
beginning to picks the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: As noted earlier, the district is run down and starting to rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shabby' rearranges AREA IF SO as AFORESAI; D comes from 'beginning to decay'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aforesaid is formal legal wording for something already referred to earlier.

clue.text: Laid up, search the internet to secure a fantastic job, wonderful for 22

indicators.note: to secure has the outer word hold the other letters inside it
laid up in a down clue means set upwards, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: to surf is to browse the internet

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something wild and fanciful, so the letters of job are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in bed browses online and lands a fantastic job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' reverses SURF to FRUS; 'fantastic' turns JOB into BJO; 'to secure' puts A plus BJO inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Frabjous is a nonsense coinage in Carroll's poem meaning splendid, joyous.

clue.text: Character also falling sick after Jack?

indicators.note: after puts the sickness letters behind the card letter

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
falling sick is becoming ill

explanation.surface: Recalls the nursery rhyme in which Jill too comes tumbling after Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'Jack and Jill', Jack fell down and Jill came tumbling after, hence 'also falling'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill is a character from the nursery rhyme, Jack's companion fetching water.

clue.text: Island captured by ordinary chap is worth a chortle

indicators.note: captured by has the chap's name hold the island inside it

parts.note: an ordinary Joe is an average man
Cos (or Kos) is a Greek island

explanation.surface: An everyday bloke taken to an island finds it amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful or humorous, so something deserving a laugh.

clue.text: Punch buffoon, grabbing bully from behind, creation of 22

parts.note: a jab is a quick punch

indicators.note: grabbing has the fool hold the other letters inside

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool

indicators.note: from behind says the word is read back to front

parts.note: to cow someone is to bully them

explanation.surface: Someone punches a fool who grabs a bully from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from behind' turns the bully word around to WOC, which 'grabbing' puts inside the buffoon; berk is mild British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jabberwock is the monster slain in Lewis Carroll's poem 'Jabberwocky'.

clue.text: Bubbly ruler in 2 15

parts.note: Krug is a brand of champagne, bubbly
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen as ruler

explanation.surface: Champagne is served to a ruler in a national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 15 is NATIONAL PARK; South Africa's Kruger National Park is named after President Paul Kruger.
explanation.definitionFit: The word Kruger completes the name of South Africa's famous game reserve, Kruger National Park.

clue.text: 22's very sharp, very sharp ultimately in test

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the spoken exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's sharpness is put to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Vorpal is Carroll's invented word for the keen-edged blade that slays the Jabberwock.

clue.text: Wheels turn for author

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: Wheels revolve, making way for a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll is the author of the Alice books and the poems behind this puzzle's theme.

clue.text: Track source on the telephone?

indicators.note: on the telephone means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the root of something is its source

explanation.surface: Trying to trace where a phone call came from.
explanation.walkthrough: ROUTE is said like ROOT in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is a track or path taken from one place to another.

clue.text: Pasture in impermissible scene

indicators.note: in places the meadow word inside the forbidden one

parts.note: tabu, a variant of taboo, means forbidden
a lea is a grassy field or pasture

explanation.surface: A meadow in a forbidden scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a picturesque scene or grouping, as in a tableau vivant.

clue.text: Soothing word, razor initially having cut you once

indicators.note: having cut says the letter slices into the old pronoun

parts.note: thee is the archaic form of you

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of razor

explanation.surface: A soothing word after a razor nick.
explanation.definitionFit: 'There, there' is a comforting expression used to soothe someone upset.

clue.text: Vessel like that burning midnight oil, dash of paraffin thrown in

parts.note: so means in that way

indicators.note: thrown in says the letter is tossed inside the other piece

parts.note: someone burning the midnight oil is up late

indicators.note: dash of picks only a little of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: An oil lamp burns late into the night, with a splash of paraffin added.
explanation.definitionFit: A soup plate is a deep dish, a vessel for serving soup.

clue.text: Talk hosted by professor, a teacher

indicators.note: hosted by says the answer is held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A talk given by a professor who is also a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to talk formally, delivering a speech.

clue.text: Bond cuddling girls, sex not entirely judged fairly

indicators.note: cuddling has the joining word wrap its arms around the other pieces

parts.note: to weld is to bond metal
lasses are girls

indicators.note: not entirely says the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: James Bond cuddles girls, though the sex doesn't fully happen, and is fairly judged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' looks like 007 but is the verb to join. SEX 'not entirely' gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well-assessed has been evaluated accurately and soundly.
